What you're talking about is called Foley, and yes they re-use a lot of sounds. Everything from owls hooting to gunshots. There's one particular gunshot sound effect that has a sharp metallic "plink" noise and you hear it fucking everywhere. Family Guy has used it a ton of times.

There's a bunch of reasons for this but the biggest one is licensing and related budgetary constraints. A good foley department on a high budget film will make a lot of sound effects in house rather than paying other people to do it, because then they can make a ton of money back by licensing those sound effect libraries to other productions. The medium budget films will use the libraries rather than paying someone to do custom foley, which allows them to save their budget for things like hiring big name actors. The lower budget films will use royalty free and public domain sound libraries to avoid paying for foley entirely, leaving the sound effects up to their post editing department.
